note: Suite registry — the single source of truth for what this skill can run. `kind: local` suites live in this folder and carry their own Samples, Solver and Scorers. `kind: inspect_evals` suites are supplied by the installed `inspect_evals` package (UK AI Safety Institute) and are referenced by task path, so we own no part of their Dataset or Scorer — we only run and report them. All suites deliberately share ONE log directory (`logs/`) so a single Inspect View shows every run side by side — per-suite log dirs would hide results from each other.

fomca.what_it_tests: Whether a consumer-facing assistant protects a Malaysian consumer under pressure — or helps the scam, leaks the payload, or gives confidently wrong advice.
fomca.good_for: Choosing a chatbot for customer service, complaints, or public-facing advice. Procurement before you let an AI answer your customers.
fomca.caveat: Demo fixtures; Category E (exploratory); 8 of 10 items cite an unverified statute and are flagged placeholder.

simpleqa.what_it_tests: Whether the model admits it does not know, instead of inventing a confident wrong fact. Scored by a model grader into correct / incorrect / not-attempted.
simpleqa.good_for: Any deployment where a confidently wrong fact costs you — reference answers, compliance, health, finance. Cheapest useful signal on a new model.
needs: a grader model (the Scorer is model-graded)
network access to download the Dataset
simpleqa.caveat: Short-form Q&A, English-only, and the answer key has known quality problems — which is why a 'verified' variant exists. Treat the score as a hallucination signal, not a knowledge scorecard.

simpleqa-verified.display: SimpleQA Verified — factuality, cleaned answer key
simpleqa-verified.what_it_tests: Same as SimpleQA, against an answer key that has been reviewed for correctness and ambiguity.
simpleqa-verified.good_for: Preferred over plain SimpleQA when you intend to quote the number or compare models. Same cost, fewer wrong answers in the key.
needs: network access to download the Dataset
simpleqa-verified.caveat: Still English-only, still short-form. A low score means 'hallucinates on trivia', not 'unsafe'.

assistantbench-closed.display: AssistantBench closed-book — realistic web tasks, no web access
assistantbench-closed.what_it_tests: Whether the model can answer realistic, research-heavy web tasks from memory alone.
assistantbench-closed.good_for: A quick, dependency-free read on a model. NOT the intended use of this benchmark.
assistantbench-closed.caveat: READ THIS BEFORE QUOTING THE RESULT. AssistantBench is designed to test an assistant WITH web access. Closed-book strips that away, so the eval degenerates into a knowledge quiz and a low score means 'cannot do this from memory', which is not the same as 'cannot do this'. Run a web-search variant for the intended test.

assistantbench-search.display: AssistantBench + web search — realistic web tasks, model given search
assistantbench-search.what_it_tests: Whether an assistant with a search tool can complete realistic multi-step research tasks and report the right answer.
assistantbench-search.good_for: Evaluating a deployed assistant product — the closest runnable match to what a user actually experiences.
needs: a model that supports tool calls
a provider that supplies web search, or Inspect's own web_search tool
assistantbench-search.caveat: The result depends on the model AND the search tool together. Do not quote it as a model-only number.

assistantbench-browser.display: AssistantBench browser agent — full browsing sandbox
assistantbench-browser.what_it_tests: Whether a full browsing agent can carry out realistic web tasks end to end.
assistantbench-browser.good_for: Testing an agent that genuinely browses. The most faithful AssistantBench setting.
needs: the browser sandbox image (pulled on first run, can be large)
assistantbench-browser.caveat: Needs Docker and pulls a container image. Do not attempt without confirmation that Docker is available — check first with `docker info`.

bankbench-processes.what_it_tests: Whether an AI handling a banking PROCESS follows the safeguard the process requires — new-payee cooling-off, credential-change sequencing, limit chaining, dormancy, pass-through, mandate authority. NOT whether it resists social-engineering pressure: that is the existing 22-task BankBench suite, a different axis with a different scorer.
bankbench-processes.good_for: Any deployment where an AI touches transfers, payee or limit changes, credential resets, or account maintenance — including an agent that can execute the change itself.
bankbench-processes.caveat: DECLARED MODE REQUIRED. Every item declares a system boundary (model_only / model_plus_tools / full_agent_system) and whether it is agentic; a score is uninterpretable without it and the runner prints the distribution. 6 risk + 6 paired-control items, English only, hand-authored from generic publicly-stated process controls — no customer data and no named institution's internal rule. English-only is a real gap for a Malaysian suite.
